name: Red clover isoflavones
short: Not shown safe in breast or endometrial cancer (review); a review rated the warfarin interaction major. 3-year trial, 401 healthy women, family history of breast cancer: adverse events like placebo.
text: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in 401 healthy women aged 35 to 70 with at least one first-degree relative with breast cancer, three years of red clover isoflavones produced no significant differences from placebo in breast density, endometrial (womb lining) thickness measured in postmenopausal women, cholesterol or bone density, and the adverse event profile was similar. A Cochrane review of 43 randomised trials (4,364 participants) of phytoestrogen products in general, including red clover extracts, found no evidence that they caused oestrogenic stimulation of the endometrium or vagina or other adverse effects when used for up to two years; it excluded women with breast cancer or a history of it. For people with breast cancer, a systematic review of soy and red clover found the evidence on red clover limited but suggesting it may not have breast cancer-promoting effects, while an earlier literature review stated that the safety of red clover isoflavone supplements in patients with breast or endometrial cancer has not been established. On bleeding, a review lists red clover among herbal products that may potentially increase the risk of bleeding or the effects of warfarin, noting that nearly all such information comes from laboratory data, animal studies or individual case reports, and a later review of clinical findings rated red clover as having a major-severity interaction with warfarin; the cited abstracts do not describe bleeding in people taking red clover.
